policy_extraction.issuing_body: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)

evidence.quote: NIST has developed a framework to better manage risks to individuals, organizations, and society associated with artificial intelligence (AI)
improve the ability to incorporate trustworthiness considerations into the design, development, use, and evaluation of AI products, services, and systems
consensus-driven, open, transparent, and collaborative process
The NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF) is intended for voluntary use
intended for voluntary use and to improve the ability to incorporate trustworthiness considerations

enforcement_authorities: NIST Information Technology Laboratory (ITL) AI Program
policy_extraction.implementation_notes: The AI RMF is explicitly intended for voluntary use. A companion Playbook, Roadmap, and Crosswalk have been published. A Generative AI Profile (NIST-AI-600-1) was released July 26, 2024. A concept note for a Critical Infrastructure Profile was released April 7, 2026. The Trustworthy and Responsible AI Resource Center was launched March 30, 2023 to facilitate implementation.

risk_framing.rationale_summary: The NIST AI RMF is primarily framed around managing risks to individuals, organizations, and society, with emphasis on trustworthiness and safety in AI products and services. Secondary frames include innovation enablement (voluntary use, building industry capacity) and fundamental rights (trustworthiness considerations).

evidence_spans.quote: NIST has developed a framework to better manage risks to individuals, organizations, and society associated with artificial intelligence
intended for voluntary use and to improve the ability to incorporate trustworthiness considerations into the design, development, use, and evaluation of AI products, services, and systems
The profile will guide critical infrastructure operators towards specific risk management practices to consider when engaging AI-enabled capabilities
